items.text: Morning light renders the Mei petals nearly translucent under the sun. Beneath the Mei tree, young Yao practice in formation.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Where is your master?

items.speaker: School of Mei Believer I
items.text: Grandmaster Heron, I believe she left to attend to some personal matters.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Erm, I think it best you no longer call me that. Your master has taken a path away from my teachings. I am now nothing more than an ordinary Daoist to you.

items.speaker: School of Mei Believer I
items.text: Oh, I see.
They exchange worried glances, but seeing the pain beneath her smile, they choose not to trouble her.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: When she returns, please tell her that I want to have a word with her here. Is there a place we could speak?

items.speaker: School of Mei Believer I
items.text: Certainly, Grand, uh, I mean, Master Heron.
White clouds drift past the sun, casting shadows eastward.
After roughly half a day, Master Rén returns to the school. Before the Mei tree, Paper Heron stands alone.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: You wish to speak with me?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I do. The day's been quiet, and I've found myself reminiscing on the old days. Would you join me for a chat beneath the Mei tree?
She smiles as she gestures toward the tree in the courtyard.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: This tree?
Master Rén glances at the red Mei tree. It's scrawny for its years. Staring up at it, she can't help but laugh coldly.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Why? There isn't much to it. It could take a thousand years before it rivals the largest Mei tree in town.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Let's just talk about the old days, eh?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: When the White Horse School attempted to subdue the Beast Lǎnzhū, they were taken by surprise by rival schools. We lost all our most capable masters in the battle.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Seeing no other way, my grandmaster shattered one of the two Longevity Swords, releasing the Qi within to create a seal. The last student of the school and the beast were frozen in that moment, sealed inside a Mei tree.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: A hundred years later, a Painted-Skin Yao faced her celestial tribulation under the same tree. Lightning struck both her and the tree, and the seal was broken.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: The lightning nearly destroyed the Yao. The White Horse student, freed from the seal and surprised by such a turn of fate, saved the dying Yao and taught her the Daoist arts. We both know the story.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Yes, you remember every detail of it.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: I could never forget.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I gave you the remaining sword and taught you the way of Inner Alchemy, but I never asked you to take the name of a White Horse student. I knew the school was lost to history.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: The school is gone, yes, but their duty to control the Xiǎndào Beast was unfinished.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: What's the purpose of this, Heron?
She shakes her head, gazing out into the distance toward another giant Mei tree far beyond their sight—a sister of the school's own centerpiece.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: What is your purpose, Rén?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You told your students to channel their Qi into the Mei tree. Why?
Her old student looks at her and simply laughs.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: So you've found out about that.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I'm not easily fooled.
Master Rén lets the words roll over her as she settles herself at the stone table beneath the tree's shadow.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: I know you disagree with my methods, but whether you agree or not, this is what is best for the students.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: They're not like you. None of them have the talent or lifespan to properly cultivate longevity.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Had you been in my place, you likely wouldn't have taken them on at all. But I want to give them a chance.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: After all, what would a talented master like you know of the life of a lowly Yao, of our struggles and desires?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I do not mean to question your teachings, Rén. I only need to know why you've focused their Qi there, of all places.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: My, my, when did you become so impatient, Heron?
*ching*
Master Rén casts a familiar incantation, and the white sword reappears in the air.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: You trusted me with the sword, and I have endeavored to honor that trust by sharing it. I was once a short-lived Yao myself. It is only natural that I wish to help my kind.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Combining Inner Alchemy with the power of the Longevity Sword, I developed a method for our kind to overcome their disadvantages.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: The sword can hold and release Qi. It gives, and it takes. Through it, I work to bring the Yao the lives they deserve.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Should they succeed, there will be one more Daoist master to carry the Method forward.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: And if they fail, their remaining Qi is gathered within the Mei tree to aid us in subduing the beast when it next awakens. Either way, the outcome is favorable.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: And either way, their deaths will not be in vain.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You lay it out so plainly. Do your students know?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Do they know their master sees them as mere fuel for her designs?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Hahaha ... Does it matter? Each one of them knows longevity comes at a price.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Do you think any of them would have joined me if they were not willing to risk their lives?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Does any price we pay matter if it means subduing the beast?
She laughs again, but there's no joy in it. Paper Heron turns her head away.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: "No matter the cost," I said. I gave you my word. This is but a small portion of the sacrifices I am prepared to make.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You also promised to do your best to care for your students.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: If the beast breaks free, every one of them will perish, whether on that fateful day or any other, they have the same choice: aid me, or else die a pointless death.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: I should hope you know me well enough to trust that I do not undertake this selfishly. Do you not see that I am doing only what must be done?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Keeping Lǎnzhū subdued will not require nearly this much Qi.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: With the Qi you've gathered, the lives you've sacrificed ...

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You could kill the beast.
At some point, the wind in the courtyard had stilled completely.
Master Rén raises her head and fixes Paper Heron with a mocking stare.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: You were given a weapon of magnificent power—the capability to sense the cycle of all things and even manipulate the wax and wane of life itself.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Yet the White Horse School merely used it to clear the blockage of Qi in Lǎnzhū. An all-powerful sword reduced to a tamer's whip.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Because Lǎnzhū must not die.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Paper Heron, you of all people, are the last I expected to say such a thing. You lost your school, your friends, your masters, to this beast, and you would have it remain a threat forever?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: What good would come of that?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: The Xiǎndào Beasts play a necessary part in the workings of Heaven. A far greater danger may come of its death, one that extends far beyond Huanzhou. Have I not taught you as much?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: And why should I follow your teachings, hm? Why should I bind my students, and their students alike, to an endless cycle of subduing the beast?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Humans have a strange attachment to their "legacies." But to be Yao is to be defined by one short life. I intend to make mine echo through the ages.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Lǎnzhū will perish and the cycle will end, and all for a small price.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: No more endless duties passed from hand to hand, no more deaths in service of legacy. Our school will never suffer as yours did.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: As for me, I will share the power released from the dead beast with my students, and together, we will ascend to immortality!
She takes a deep breath. As she opens her eyes again, her voice is cold as winter.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: This goes against the Way. It isn't natural.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: What does it mean for a thing to be natural?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Would it not have been natural for you to let me die under that Mei tree?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: But you didn't. My very life is proof that the Way can be defied.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Perhaps there is risk in diverting the cycles of Heaven. But how much greater are the rewards?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: If there is risk, I take it gladly. I will slay the beast and free Huanzhou and its people from its threat.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Then, I will ascend.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: And if you fail? What will happen to the people?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: I won't fail.
Silence follows, broken by the returning wind as it rustles the Mei tree's branches.
Master Rén doesn't betray a hint of doubt, but her former master's reply comes like a sharp cut.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Your pride has blinded you.
Suddenly, arcane light flashes before Master Rén's eyes.
She raises her brush in defense but is driven back a dozen steps.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Hahaha. Are you really the same woman I called Master? All I have done is speak honestly, yet you answer with a lethal strike!

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: You lecture me about pride, then dare to take my life?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: But if you choose to stand in my way, then I must take yours!

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Heh! Hah!

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Have I trained you so poorly?
Paper Heron strikes at Master Rén's weak point, but her opponent abandons resistance, instead raising the Longevity Sword like a hostage.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: What?

Caught off guard, Paper Heron is forced to withdraw her attack mid-strike. She barely retrieves the Longevity Sword, leaving a scar on the sheath. Yet she cannot escape the backlash of her own arcane skill.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Hahahaha ...

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Why do you stay your hand, Heron? Strike me down, if you truly believe it to be just! Or is it that you care more for this sword than any living thing?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: You have lost more than your senses, Master. Make whatever claims you like, but I see your empty heart. All that matters to you is your legacy, your mission! And I was only a tool.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Are you now too blind to see how deep your hypocrisy runs?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Enough.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: *cough*
Master Rén clutches her chest and coughs up blood.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: All the decades I have given in preparation. You cannot stop me now, not when I am this close to success!
She raises her brush, gathering energy as veins bulge on her forehead. At last, she lunges at her in a furious charge.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: What?
Paper Heron retreats a step but fails to evade the attack entirely. Sharp pain tears through her chest.
Seeing that Master Rén shows no sign of relenting, Paper Heron has no choice but to cast another incantation.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Hmm?
The smoke clears. Before Master Rén stands only a paper figure clutching a sword.

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Hmph.

items.speaker: All Yao
items.text: Master! Should we go after her?

items.speaker: Master Ren
items.text: Go. Whether dead or alive, she must not escape with the Longevity Sword. Bring it to me intact!

items.speaker: All Yao
items.text: Yes, Master.
The Yao scatter.
She casts one final sneering glance at the scrawny Mei tree in the courtyard, then flicks her sleeves and leaves.
